27.08.2026 | Found in board-dry code audit of the new 4-step signup quiz (2bebce1).

â€¢ The quiz answers (username, full name, country, region, availability) are parked in localStorage cc_pending_signup right before signUp()/OAuth, then auto-applied with NO form shown once the account exists (CompleteProfileView).
â€¢ It was never expired and only cleared on a successful completeProfile(). An abandoned quiz (closed the verify-email tab, cancelled Google OAuth) left the blob sitting there.
â€¢ Next person to create an account in that browser -- a club tablet, a family PC, someone signing up with Google from the Log In tab -- had the stranger's username/name/location silently written to THEIR profile.

Fix shipped:
â€¢ cc_pending_signup now carries a savedAt timestamp; peekPendingSignup() ignores + clears anything older than 1h (real email-confirm / OAuth round-trips finish in seconds-to-minutes).
â€¢ Existing-account paths (email login, Log In tab Google/Facebook) now clear any leftover pending blob before authenticating.
â€¢ Added selfcheck coverage in utils.selfcheck.ts.

Board was dry (only the 2 long-blocked video-tooling items left), so per Step 2b ran a code-audit subagent. Found and fixed 2 real bugs, same root-cause class as the ctxUser.uid bug fixed earlier today (a correct pattern applied everywhere except one call site):

2) The "Suggested" players card on /players linked real users via raw /players/${username}/ (404s, static export) instead of the existing profileHref() helper that every other call site in the app already uses for exactly this reason. One-line fix.

npx next build clean, deployed (commit 3676f80), verified live by fetching the deployed JS chunks and confirming both the new regex and profileHref() output are present in the served bundle.

13.08.2026 (1pm, auto-dev, code audit): unregisterTournament (AppContext.tsx:918-927) computes currentPlayers: Math.max(0, t.currentPlayers - 1) from a possibly-stale local snapshot and writes it directly via updateTournamentDoc -- a plain read-modify-write. registerForTournament/approveTournamentRequest deliberately route through the atomic register_tournament_participant RPC to avoid exactly this race (see comment at supabaseService.ts:927-933, from a prior audit fix), but withdrawal never got the same treatment. Two concurrent withdrawals, or a withdrawal racing a registration, can under/over-count currentPlayers and drift the displayed capacity from reality. Fix: add an atomic unregister_tournament_participant RPC (decrement + remove from participants in one transaction), mirroring migration 0026's register function. Lower priority than the overbooking direction (P2, already closed) since undercounting capacity is a display glitch, not a data-integrity/security issue. Not yet fixed.

13.08.2026 (5pm, auto-dev): Fixed -- added unregister_tournament_participant (migration 0029), mirrors register_tournament_participant's SELECT...FOR UPDATE locking. Client falls back to the old read-modify-write if the RPC errors as not-found, so withdrawal keeps working until Lok runs 0029 in the Supabase SQL editor -- once applied it auto-switches to the atomic path, no further deploy needed. Build clean, deployed (commit 53c7f30).

Confirmed applied + correctly restricted via anon-key probe on unregister_tournament_participant -- 42501 permission denied (function exists, anon denied), same verification method used for 0026/0027/0028. text.content: Self-caused bug: 0026's grant execute ... to authenticated was redundant -- Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default on new functions unless explicitly revoked, and 0026 never revoked it. Confirmed live via curl with only the anon key: register_tournament_participant and add_club_member_atomic both returned 200 false (call allowed) instead of a permission error. Both are SECURITY DEFINER (bypass RLS by design), so this meant an unauthenticated caller could mutate tournament/club data directly -- undoing part of tonight's RLS lockdown. supabase/migrations/0027_revoke_public_execute.sql fixes it: revoke execute ... from public on both functions, doesn't touch the authenticated grant. Re-verify after running: curl the RPC endpoints with only the anon apikey/Authorization header, should now get a permission-denied error instead of 200 false.

text.content: Found during 5pm code audit while reviewing yesterday's (08.08) live-session features that hadn't been through an auto-dev pass yet. Root cause: loadUserProfile does select('*'), so weekly_digest_sent_at (migration 0022 still not applied by Lok) always comes back undefined from Supabase. The onAuthStateChanged hydrate effect in AppContext.tsx spread the full profile object (including this undefined key) over local state on every login/reload, wiping the good value that updateUser had already cached in localStorage - so the 7-day digest cadence never actually held, it re-sent on every fresh session load. Fixed at the hydrate site: filter out undefined-valued keys from the loaded profile before merging, so a not-yet-migrated column can no longer clobber a locally-cached value (protects any future column in the same situation, not just this one). npx next build clean, deployed (commit a350a94), verified live - no console errors, normal data loads. Does not remove the need for Lok to eventually run supabase/migrations/0022_weekly_digest.sql so the sent-at timestamp persists server-side too; this fix only stops the local clobbering, cadence will still be approximate (resets on every device swap) until that migration runs.

text.content: Found in code audit: registerTournament (AppContext.tsx) and approveTournamentRequest (supabaseService.ts) both incremented currentPlayers/appended participants with no check against maxPlayers - unlike the club-join path, which already enforces max_members server-side. Two people grabbing the last spot at once (or a stale UI) could push currentPlayers past maxPlayers, breaking the capacity bar. Fix: added registerForTournament() in supabaseService.ts that re-reads the live row and rejects if full (same fetch-check-write shape as addClubMember's max_members guard), wired it into registerTournament with a rollback + 'Event Full' notification on rejection, and added the same check to approveTournamentRequest with a decline notification if the event filled up while the request was pending. Deployed commit bf963b2.
